name: The North
climate: Harsh subarctic winters, brief summers; permafrost dominates the deep north
description: The largest of the Seven Kingdoms by land area and the least forgiving by temperament. North of the Neck stretches a continent of ancient pines, frozen lakes, and skies that turn dark for months at a time. The North breeds a particular kind of human — one who does not complain about hardship because hardship is simply Tuesday. Castle Black and the Wall mark the edge of the known world; beyond lies something older than kingdoms, older than memory.

name: King's Landing
climate: Temperate maritime; warm summers, mild winters, persistent sea winds
description: The capital of the Seven Kingdoms squats on the banks of the Blackwater Rush where it meets Blackwater Bay, a city of half a million souls crammed behind walls that were built for a far smaller population. Its streets smell of salt, sewage, and ambition. The Red Keep crowns Aegon's Hill like a scar, and the Iron Throne within it has been the most expensive seat in Westeros — paid for in blood by every generation that coveted it.

name: The Reach
climate: Fertile temperate; long growing seasons, ample rainfall, mild winters
description: The breadbasket of Westeros, where the land itself seems to have decided to be generous. The Reach produces more food than any other region, its golden fields stretching in every direction from the towers of Highgarden. It is the most populous region, the wealthiest after the Westerlands, and its lords have the dangerous habit of confusing comfort with security.

name: Dorne
climate: Hot and arid; desert interior, more temperate coastline, year-round warmth
description: The southernmost kingdom is also the most singular — in culture, law, and temperament. Dorne practices equal inheritance regardless of gender, permits bastard children greater dignity than the rest of the realm, and produces a people who have historically been impossible to conquer. The sun beats down on red sand mountains and bone-dry riverbeds, and the Dornish have absorbed that heat into their character — passionate, stubborn, and capable of carrying a grievance for decades without forgetting a single detail.

name: The Vale of Arryn
climate: Alpine; cold mountain winters, cool summers, heavy snow at elevation
description: The Vale is defended by the most effective fortification in the known world — the mountains themselves. The Giant's Lance and its surrounding peaks have protected the Vale from every invasion in its history, with the Bloody Gate serving as the one passage through. Tucked behind these natural walls, the Vale has enjoyed a prosperity and insularity that has made its lords both secure and, perhaps, slightly detached from the realities afflicting the rest of the realm.

name: The Iron Islands
climate: Cold maritime; perpetually storm-lashed, salt spray and grey skies, rarely warm
description: Seven wind-scoured islands in Ironman's Bay, where the sea has stripped everything down to the essential. The ironborn who survive here develop the same quality — stripped of softness, forged in salt water and storm. Their culture celebrates what they call the Old Way: taking what others build, reaving what others harvest, worshipping a god who dwells in drowning. A people defined entirely by what they are willing to do to survive.

name: The Riverlands
climate: Temperate continental; fertile floodplains, river mists, variable seasons
description: The crossroads of Westeros in every sense — geographically, politically, and militarily. Every army that marches between north and south must cross the Riverlands, and the rivers that give the region its name have also given it its history: a thousand years of being marched across, fought over, burned, rebuilt, and marched across again. Riverrun stands at the confluence of the Tumblestone and Red Fork, a castle that has absorbed more war than any other.

name: The Stormlands
climate: Maritime storm-prone; heavy rainfall, dramatic seasonal swings, coastal tempests
description: Named for the ferocious storms that roll in from Shipbreaker Bay and the Narrow Sea, the Stormlands build men in the image of their weather — sudden, violent, and capable of surprising calm between the episodes of fury. Storm's End, the great castle of House Baratheon, has weathered every storm the gods have sent for eight thousand years. That durability is the Stormlands in architectural form.

name: Essos
climate: Varies dramatically: from the tundra of the far east to the tropical Jade Sea coast
description: The great continent across the Narrow Sea, vast beyond Westerosi comprehension, cradle of civilizations that make the Seven Kingdoms look young and provisional. Essos contains the Free Cities — mercantile republics born from the ruins of old Valyria — the endless grass of the Dothraki Sea, the ancient slave cities of Slaver's Bay, and beyond them the mysteries of the far east that even the most traveled maesters know only from rumor.
